newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore EDB sees growth in co-investment efforts.
newsitem.headline: Singapore EDB sees growth in co-investment efforts.

text.p: Singapore's Economic Development Board (EDB) said on Monday it has made steady progress in joint investments with multi-nationals and local companies and there are plans to increase funds under its management.
EDB Investments, the EDB's investment arm, manages a total of Singapore $1.3 billion, the EDB said in a statement.
It said S$227.6 million was committed to seven projects under the Cluster Development Fund (CDF), one of several funds under EDB Investments.
Since the launch of the CDF in December 1993, S$483.4 million has been committed to 15 projects.
The Regional Investment Company (RIC), another unit of EDB Investments, invested S$8.93 million in three projects last year, and manages an S$82 million fund.
EDB said its programme aimed to strengthen partnerships by co-investing with multi-national corporations and local firms in risk-sharing ventures both in and outside Singapore.
